plan: A kirtan: one voice calls and the room answers. par_15 is the singer's lamp all show long — it follows whoever is leading, and at 112s it is the only thing lit. Saffron is the leader, rose the responders, indigo the room, white reserved for the three arrivals: the D-major hinge at bar 15, the chorus landing at bar 23, and the loudest bar of the song at bar 47, which is set up by half a second of black.

states.why: Bars 2-3 are lead-vocal, vocal and cello at 25-36% loud. Two lamps at a whisper on the ends of the rig. Nothing covers bars 0-1 at all, so the show opens in real darkness and the voice brings the light up.
Bar 4 is percussion and congas, 7 hits — the first time anything is struck. The light starts to travel, on the outer pair only, so the inner stays dark and the widening is visible.
Bars 6-8 are wind, trombone, tuba and brass — held tones, no drums (1 hit a bar). A held wash is what horns look like; all four lamps for the first time.
The floor under the spotlight at bar 9, and what the room falls back to once the isolate lets go.
Bars 11-12 are violin, timpani and viola at 51/43%. Moving but small: the travelling figure on the inner pair only.

Bar 13 is 55% loud with ZERO drum onsets — a sustained vocal and synth pad with no rhythm in it. Two lamps at a whisper. It ends at bar 14, and nothing covers bar 14 at all: at 26% loud and still no hits, it is the emptiest bar of the first half, so the room goes out before the hinge rather than dimming politely through it.

Bar 15 is the hinge of the first half: harmony turns D:min to D major, hits jump 0 to 12 a bar, guitar/strings/acoustic-guitar all enter. Every beat hits from here, and stagger 0.45 sends it left-to-right across the rig rather than four lamps in lockstep.

Bars 19-21 are the instrumental's own peak (63/61/68%, strings and bass on top). A full-rig travelling pulse, one bump per beat, climbing into the chorus. Bar 22 is deliberately left with NO state — it is the producer's gap.
Bars 23-29 are the chorus proper, 67-78% loud with 10-12 hits a bar, kick and snare and tambourine. Saffron against indigo: the leader against the room.
Bar 30 drops to 48% between two 74%+ bars — kick falls to 0.16, tambourine to 0.11. A 33-second section has to breathe somewhere and this is the place the music picked.

Bars 31-35 are the call-and-response: lead-vocal and back-vocal measure -0.75 correlated here, back taking bars 32-34 (0.42/0.65/0.63) while lead falls to 0.23. Rose leads the pair colours because the responders are carrying it, and stagger 0.58 makes the figure cross the room like the answer does.
Bars 36-37 the leader is back alone (lead 0.64/0.60, back 0.05/0.07). The room narrows to the two inner lamps in saffron and holds — a look kept for four seconds, which is the point.
Bar 38 is a real dropout: strings 0.15, guitar 0.18, kick 0.12, only synth at 0.60. 50% loud between two 85% bars. An ember on two lamps.

The second chorus opens travelling rather than hammering — bars 39-42 run 79-86% with back-vocal taking over from the lead (lead falls to mean 0.10 here, back rises to 0.59). Rose, because the responders own this section.

Bars 43-46 are toms, drums and back-vocal at 85-90% — loud, but bar 47 is 92% and has to be brighter still, so this bed sits a step below the one that follows it. Every beat hits, stagger 0.40 sends it across the rig.

96.3-97.8s: the whole rig held at near-full white for one bar. No travel, no beat — the brightest STILL look in the show, sitting on the front of the loudest 5-second window so the hit that follows has somewhere to come from.

Bar 47 is the single loudest bar of the song at 92%. The brightest bed in the show, at full amount with the floor held high. It stops at bar 48, which is the 80% dip between two 85%+ bars — so the rig's own brightest five seconds sits on bar 47 rather than trailing across the come-down.
Bars 48-51 come down (80-85%) and turn to piano, keys, woodwind, harmonica and flute. Half the pulse rate and warm: still moving, no longer hammering.
The last bar of the last chorus stops moving and holds one colour, so the spin over it reads as a flourish and not as more of the same.
Bar 53 has zero drum onsets and falls to 37%. The track strips back and so does the rig — the outer pair only, which also keeps the two centre lamps from carrying more of this show than the ends do.
Bar 54 has NO state at all — that is the void, and it is meant to be black. Bar 55 is the band back for two seconds (bass 0.88, strings 0.72) before the singer leaves for good.
Bars 56-57: the voice has gone and it is harp, banjo and strings. All four lamps, but barely on — the quietest full-rig look in the show.
The music moves up an octave at 120.29s and the harmony turns to D major at 120.0. Strings run 0.80/0.80/0.91 across bars 58-60 — the outro's real peak. The room moves again, warm.
Bar 61 is one drum hit and a last vocal line. Two lamps, held, nothing travelling.
Every one of the 39 lanes reads 0.00 from 127.15s. One ember on the singer's lamp for two bars, then no state at all — the show ends in real darkness, not a fade.

bindings.why: par_15 is the singer's lamp for the whole show. It starts here: lead-vocal is median 0.36 across the intro, so the middle lamp breathes with the invocation while the others hold the bed.
No voice in the instrumental — strings carry it (median 0.72, above-0.5 for 60% of the section). Same lamp, new leader.
The leader is back and above 0.5 for half the section. Bound to one lamp rather than the rig so the drive bed keeps the other three on the beat.
The handover, in one lamp: lead-vocal falls to mean 0.10 here and back-vocal rises to 0.59. The lamp that was the leader's becomes the responders'.
back-vocal is above 0.5 for 100% of this section. A high floor because this lamp sits inside the song's loudest passage and must not be the dark one there.
Strings are the outro (mean 0.53, 0.91 by bar 60). Floor 0 so this lamp is genuinely out through the void at bar 54 instead of hovering at a few DMX.

gestures.why: The first sound in the song is the lead vocal at 0.4s. The room is black until bar 1 and then blooms saffron with him — the invocation. It also gives the opening ten seconds a shape; the first bake held a flat drone there for 9.8 unbroken seconds, which is the one thing a show cannot afford at the top.

Bar 2 carries 5 drum onsets — more than bars 1 and 3 together — under vocal, lead-vocal and bass. One saffron step on the centre pair as the swell falls away, so the ten seconds of drone that follow read as a look being held rather than a rig that has stalled.
Moment 0, build at 9.11s: the drums thicken, bar 4 jumps from 1 hit to 7. Small, partial, on the downbeat.
One beat of nothing to set up the biggest thing in the intro. Darkness is the cheapest way to make a small hit read as large.

Moment 1, intensity 1.00 at 13.83s: synth and back-vocal enter and the harmony turns to A at 13.89. Full-rig white for one beat — the biggest thing SO FAR, not the biggest in the song, which is why it is a stab and not an impact.
The hit opens into a bloom. A swell's envelope is ~0 at its own anchor, so it starts a beat after the stab rather than on top of it.
Moment 2 at 17.75s: the tempo map really does step 89.341 to 118.77 bpm at 17.27s. 1 to 1.33 is that ratio — the lighting's pulse rate shifts by exactly what the music's did.
Moment 3, spotlight 0.93 at 21.80s — everything drops back behind lead-vocal. rest 0 so the other three lamps are truly off, not at 5 DMX; on a four-lamp rig that is the only way isolation reads.
Bar 12 is the last struck bar before two bars with no drum onsets at all. One step so the quiet that follows is a decision, not a stall.
Moment 4, pause 0.73 at 33.0s. Bar 14 is 26% loud with zero hits — the track's own blackout. Two beats of real black ending exactly on bar 15.

The first of three white arrivals. D:min turns to D major at 33.80s, drum hits go 0 to 12, guitar and strings and acoustic-guitar all enter on this downbeat. It gets the beat to itself so nothing caps its attack.
Instrumental with no voice — the head takes the lead and sweeps the room while the pars hold the drive bed underneath. beam touches only the head, so the bed is not interrupted.

Bar 21 is the loudest bar of the instrumental at 68%. A rise that holds rather than returns, aimed straight at the gap in bar 22. over_beats and for_beats match, or the rise finishes early and drops back.
Moment 5, pause 0.77 at 48.0s: bar 22 falls to 39% between a 68% and a 73% bar. No state covers this bar, so the room is black between the strobes — accelerating white pops into the chorus.
The chorus lands. Bar 23 is 73% with kick, guitar and electric-guitar — the first bar of the song that is genuinely full.

Moment 6, climax 1.00 at 52.76s — the whole band, six families at once. A hardware strobe rather than a second impact, because the same gesture twice in two bars reads as a repeat rather than an escalation.
Bar 27 is the chorus's own high point at 78%, tambourine and lead-vocal on top. Punctuation, not an event.
The mid-chorus dip. Levels fall away for exactly the two seconds the music does, then the responders come in on bar 31.

Call and response, placed where it actually happens: lead 0.32 to back 0.42 at bar 32, lead 0.29 to back 0.65 at bar 33. Saffron on the left hands the room to rose on the right over four seconds. trade is the one effect that lights the whole rig and still has the lamps doing different things.

Moment 7, entrance 0.70 at 72.25s — the lead comes back in. Bar 34 beat 4 is 72.27s on the measured grid, so this lands on it. Saffron on the LEFT pair: the leader takes the room back, and he takes back the side he handed away at bar 32. A stab rather than a second trade, because trade only ever runs left to right and this goes the other way.
Bar 38's dropout, emptied from the edges in. A controlled pull-back rather than a blackout, because the synth is still there at 0.60 and the music has not actually stopped.
The handover for good, on the section boundary. From bar 39 the lead never comes back above 0.23 and back-vocal runs 0.42-0.79 to the end of the choruses.
The harmony steps to C at 85.83s. A white flick on the two outer lamps marks the turn without taking the room.
Toms and drums enter on bar 43 (89%). A partial impact — the inner pair only — so the full-rig one four bars later still has somewhere to go.
One beat of nothing so the hit on the peak has something to arrive out of.

Moment 9, peak 1.00 at 92.5s — the loudest single 0.5s sample in the recording. Two lamps, white, straight out of the cut on the beat before: against a drive bed that is already hitting every beat, a partial hit only reads if the room was taken away first. It is deliberately NOT the full rig — that belongs to bar 47, where the loudest five seconds actually are.

The song's loudest five seconds are centred on 97.0s — I computed that from acoustic.loudness rather than trusting the brief's 92.5s headline, which is the loudest single 0.5s sample and a different claim. A white bloom from 95.8s cresting at 97.6s puts the rig's own brightest stretch on the recording's. The blackout and the impact punch straight through it, because a gesture started later wins the fixture.
Half a second of black at 97.27s, inside the loudest passage in the song. Nothing else reads against a full room — a stab under a full drive bed is invisible, so the room has to be taken away first.

The biggest gesture in the show, on bar 47 — 92% loud, the single loudest bar, and the bar the loudest 5s window (centred 97.0s, computed from acoustic.loudness) runs into. Full rig, full white, straight out of the black.
Moment 10, build 0.32 at 101.25s: kick and digital-piano thicken into bar 50.

Woodwind, harmonica and flute take bar 51 — the last instrumental voice in the choruses. The head snaps corner to corner over the pulse bed rather than adding more brightness to a section that is already full.

Spend-once, to close the last chorus — one second on the last two beats of bar 52, two full hue turns. Kept to a second because spin lights the whole rig at ~230 DMX and a two-bar version made 107.8s the brightest passage of the show, which belongs at 97.0s.
Moment 11, breakdown 0.53 at 109.76s — exactly this downbeat. Zero drum onsets in bar 53. The room empties on a settle.
Moment 12, pause 0.85. This is the honest isolate of the song: at 112.0-113.0s lead-vocal reads 0.40/0.33 and EVERY other lane is 0.00-0.04. One voice, one lamp, three lamps off.
The voice falls to 0.11 at 113.0s — the quietest instant in the song, loudness 0.022. The last lamp goes out too. Nothing is lit for half a second.
Bass hits 0.88 at 114.0s with strings and acoustic-guitar — the band is back, briefly. A bloom out of the black, not a bang: the music does not slam here, it returns.
Moment 13, exit 1.00 at 115.29s: lead-vocal, tambourine and vocal all drop out together. The room quiets to a fifth. This is the last the singer is heard until bar 60.
Harp, banjo and strings alone with the pars nearly out. The beam is the only thing moving, which is the point — a four-lamp rig at drone level has no motion of its own to give.

Bar 57 is 54% loud against bar 56's 32% — the strings step up to 0.68 on their way to 0.80 and 0.91. Two lamps for two beats, so the four seconds of drone either side of it are a held look rather than a dead one.

Moment 14, register_shift 1.00 at 120.29s, and the harmony turns to D major at 120.0. The only tier-one gesture that does not return, because the music went UP and stayed there; tilt lifts with it. `by` is held to 0.26 because at 0.42 this three-second hold became the brightest five seconds in the show, and the outro of a bhajan is not that.

Moment 15, entrance 1.00 at 123.77s — lead-vocal and vocal return over the outro's loudest bar (strings 0.91, dobro 0.81). The call-and-response figure comes back one last time to close it: saffron hands across to gold. A trade rather than a swell because a swell always blooms to full white level, and nothing in the outro may be brighter than bar 47.
Moment 16, rhythm_change at 126.71s — the beat drops away, bar 61 has one hit and bar 62 has none. One beat of nothing, and then the drone ember is all that is left.
